questions.question: The SI unit of electric charge is the:
questions.explanation: 1 ampere = 1 coulomb per second.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Current is measured in:
questions.explanation: Therapeutic currents are in milliamperes (mA) or microamperes (µA).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Potential difference is measured in:
questions.explanation: One volt is one joule of work per coulomb of charge.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: The unit of electrical resistance is the:
questions.explanation: Conductance is measured in siemens (mho).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: The unit of capacitance is the:
questions.explanation: Inductance is measured in henries; magnetic flux density in tesla.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Frequency is measured in:
questions.explanation: One hertz is one cycle per second.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Two resistors of 10 Ω and 20 Ω connected in series have a total resistance of:
questions.explanation: Series: R = R1 + R2. Parallel: 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Two identical resistors of 10 Ω connected in parallel have a total resistance of:
questions.explanation: For identical resistors R/2; total resistance in parallel is always less than the smallest.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Electrical power in watts equals:
questions.explanation: P = VI = I²R = V²/R.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Direct current (DC) is a current that:
questions.explanation: Mains supply in India is alternating current of 230 V at 50 Hz.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: The frequency of the mains alternating current supply in India is:
questions.explanation: The USA uses 60 Hz.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Which of the following is a good electrical conductor?
questions.explanation: Insulators: rubber, glass, plastic, dry air.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Which tissue is the best conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Tissues with high water and electrolyte content conduct best (blood, muscle, nerve); fat, bone and dry skin are poor conductors.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: The electromotive force (EMF) of a cell is:

options.C: The potential drop across the load
options.D: The potential difference across the terminals when no current is drawn

questions.explanation: Terminal potential difference falls below the EMF when current flows because of internal resistance.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: A transistor is mainly used in electrotherapy apparatus as a:
questions.explanation: Semiconductor devices have replaced thermionic valves.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: A thyristor is used in electrotherapy circuits as a:
questions.explanation: It can regulate the power delivered by a circuit.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: A residual current device (RCD/ELCB) protects against electric shock by:

options.C: Breaking the circuit when it detects leakage current to earth

questions.explanation: Trips typically at 30 mA within milliseconds.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Patient circuits in therapeutic equipment are isolated from the mains by:
questions.explanation: Isolation reduces the risk of a shock path through the patient to earth.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Which electrode material is commonly used for electrotherapy because it is flexible and conductive?
questions.explanation: Used with a conductive gel or moist pad; metal foil electrodes can be used with lint pads.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Current density beneath an electrode is increased by:

options.D: Reducing the size of the electrode

questions.explanation: Current density = current / area; the active electrode is smaller.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Pulse duration in electrical stimulation refers to:

options.C: The number of pulses per second
options.D: The time from the beginning to the end of a single pulse

questions.explanation: Frequency is pulses per second; the interpulse interval is the gap.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: In neuromuscular electrical stimulation, a ramp-up time is used to:

options.B: Gradually increase intensity for a more comfortable contraction

questions.explanation: Typically 1–2 seconds ramp-up, 5–10 s on-time, 1–2 s ramp-down.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: A typical on:off ratio for NMES used to strengthen muscle is about:

options.A: 1:5 (e.g. 10 s on and 50 s off) to prevent fatigue

questions.explanation: Short contraction times and long rests reduce fatigue.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: A frequency of about 35–50 Hz in NMES typically produces:
questions.explanation: Frequencies below ~20 Hz give individual twitches.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: The ‘motor point’ of a muscle is:

options.B: The point where the motor nerve enters the muscle and the lowest stimulus threshold is found

questions.explanation: Stimulating over the motor point gives the greatest contraction for the least current.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: To stimulate a denervated muscle effectively, the pulse duration should be:

options.B: Long (tens to hundreds of milliseconds) with a slow rise

questions.explanation: Denervated fibres respond to long-duration current; short pulses require unacceptable intensity.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: EMG biofeedback is used to:

options.D: Give the patient auditory or visual information about muscle activity to enhance control

questions.explanation: Used for muscle re-education, relaxation and in stroke.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Microcurrent (MENS) therapy delivers current in the range of:
questions.explanation: Used on wounds and soft tissue healing; evidence is limited.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Burst (pulse-train) TENS consists of:

options.B: Bursts of high-frequency pulses delivered at low frequency (about 2–4 bursts/s)

questions.explanation: Combines low-rate endorphin effect with comfortable high-frequency pulses.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: In conventional TENS for pain relief, electrodes should be placed:

options.B: Over or around the painful area, or over the relevant dermatome/nerve proximal to the pain

questions.explanation: Crossing the heart is avoided.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Habituation (accommodation) to TENS can be reduced by:

options.B: Varying the frequency or intensity periodically (modulation)

questions.explanation: Reduced efficacy may occur over time.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Dexamethasone sodium phosphate is delivered by iontophoresis from the:
questions.explanation: The phosphate-bound drug is negatively charged.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Skin burns under the electrodes in iontophoresis are caused by:

options.B: Chemical (acid/alkali) reaction produced by DC electrolysis if buffering is inadequate or current density is high

questions.explanation: Use buffered electrodes and lower current density; check sensation.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Direct (galvanic) current is contraindicated in patients with:

options.C: Metal implants in the field and impaired skin sensation

questions.explanation: Also over broken skin and in cardiac pacemakers.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: In interferential therapy, the carrier frequency typically used is about:
questions.explanation: Higher carrier frequency gives lower skin impedance but less pronounced neural stimulation.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: The ‘sweep’ (frequency modulation) in interferential current is used to:

options.A: Vary the beat frequency to reduce accommodation

questions.explanation: Typical sweep 80–150 Hz for pain.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: The diadynamic current ‘CP’ (courte période) is the:

options.A: Rapid alternation of MF and DF currents

questions.explanation: LP is a slow modulation of MF and DF; RS is rhythmic syncopation.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: The diadynamic current MF (monophasé fixé) has a frequency of:
questions.explanation: DF is 100 Hz full-wave.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Under the anode in galvanic current application the tissues become:

options.C: Acidic with decreased excitability and vasoconstriction

questions.explanation: The anode is used for analgesia and hardening of tissue; the cathode softens tissue and increases blood flow.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Under the cathode in galvanic current application there is:

options.C: Increased excitability, vasodilatation and softening of tissue

questions.explanation: Alkaline reaction (NaOH) is more irritant to the skin.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Dosage of continuous SWD is graded according to the patient's perception as dose I, II, III, IV. Dose II is:
questions.explanation: Dose I: no perceptible heat; II: just perceptible; III: moderate; IV: strong but tolerable heat.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: In subacute inflammation SWD should be given in:

options.A: A low dose (I or II) or pulsed mode

questions.explanation: High doses increase inflammation.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: The usual duration of a shortwave diathermy session is about:
questions.explanation: Depending on the dose and condition.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Shortwave diathermy over the abdomen or low back in pregnancy is:
questions.explanation: Heat and field exposure may harm the fetus.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Before applying infrared radiation, the therapist should always:

options.A: Cover the area with a metal sheet
options.D: Test skin sensation to heat and cold

questions.explanation: Impaired thermal sensation is a contraindication.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: The infrared lamp is usually placed at a distance of:
questions.explanation: Distance is adjusted according to the lamp rating and patient warmth.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: The main physiological effect of infrared radiation on the skin is:

options.D: Vasodilatation (erythema ab igne with chronic exposure)

questions.explanation: Mottled pigmentation can result from repeated exposure.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: The hot-quartz mercury vapour lamp requires warm-up before use to:
questions.explanation: About 5–10 minutes; cooling is needed before re-striking.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: During UV irradiation both patient and therapist must wear:
questions.explanation: Conjunctivitis (photokeratitis) results from unprotected exposure.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Which drug may increase sensitivity to UV radiation?
questions.explanation: Check medications before UV irradiation.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: The alpine sun lamp is used for:

options.D: General irradiation using non-contact exposure at about 45–100 cm

questions.explanation: A high-pressure mercury arc lamp emitting UVA, UVB and UVC.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: UV therapy for acne vulgaris produces its beneficial effect through:
questions.explanation: Used in a dose of E2.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: In rickets, ultraviolet radiation is beneficial because it:

options.A: Promotes synthesis of vitamin D in the skin

questions.explanation: UVB converts 7-dehydrocholesterol to cholecalciferol.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: For chronic tendon lesions, which continuous ultrasound intensity is generally used?
questions.explanation: Acute lesions: pulsed low-intensity (0.1–0.5 W/cm²).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: A general rule for ultrasound treatment duration is about:

options.A: 1–2 minutes per area equal to the size of the transducer face (ERA)

questions.explanation: Treat areas up to 2–3 times the ERA per session.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: During ultrasound application the transducer head should be:

options.B: Moved continuously with slow overlapping strokes

questions.explanation: Stationary technique causes hot spots and periosteal pain.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Standing waves in ultrasound treatment are avoided by:
questions.explanation: Standing waves can cause endothelial damage and stasis of blood cells.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: The half-value depth of ultrasound is:

options.B: The depth at which the intensity falls to half its surface value
options.C: The depth reached by the beam

questions.explanation: It decreases with increasing frequency.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) is used to:

options.B: Accelerate healing of fresh fractures and non-unions

questions.explanation: Typical output 30 mW/cm², 1.5 MHz, 20 min/day.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Therapeutic lasers used in physiotherapy are typically:
questions.explanation: Class 4 lasers heat and cut tissue and need strict safety measures.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Low-level laser therapy is believed to promote healing by:

options.A: Photochemical (photobiomodulation) effects such as increased ATP and cell proliferation

questions.explanation: Mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase absorbs red/NIR light.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Which is a contraindication to laser therapy?

options.D: Direct irradiation of the eyes and over malignant tissue

questions.explanation: Also pregnancy (over the abdomen) and photosensitive patients.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: The grid (point-by-point) method of laser application is used for:

options.B: Small lesions or points, with the probe in contact over each spot

questions.explanation: Scanning is used for large areas with the probe held 1–2 cm away.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Pulsed electromagnetic field (PEMF) therapy is used to:

options.A: Promote bone healing and relieve pain at low-intensity magnetic fields

questions.explanation: Not used with pacemakers or in pregnancy.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Extracorporeal shockwave therapy is commonly used for:

options.C: Chronic plantar fasciitis, calcific tendinitis of the shoulder and lateral epicondylitis

questions.explanation: Shockwaves are acoustic pulses with high peak pressure.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Ice massage is applied for:

options.D: 5–10 minutes with slow circular strokes until numbness

questions.explanation: Stages: cold, burning, aching, numbness.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: The characteristic sequence of sensations during cold application is:
questions.explanation: Numbness appears at about 12–15 minutes.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Vapocoolant (ethyl chloride) spray is used with stretch in:
questions.explanation: The spray provides a cold stimulus that inhibits pain while the muscle is stretched.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: Cold water immersion at about 10–15 °C is typically used for:

options.A: Acute sprain of the distal extremity

questions.explanation: Duration about 10–15 minutes.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: The usual temperature range for a warm whirlpool for a limb is:
questions.explanation: Whole-body Hubbard tank water is kept near 35–37 °C.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: A Hubbard tank is used for:

options.A: Full-body immersion with space to move the limbs

questions.explanation: A Lowboy whirlpool is for the limbs.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy

questions.question: The optimal pH of water in a therapeutic pool is about:
questions.explanation: Chlorine 1–3 ppm; irritation of eyes and skin occurs outside this range.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
